diagrams.title: Neutrophilic Dermatoses Treatment by Phenotype
diagrams.subtitle: Treatment selection follows morphology, severity, diagnostic certainty, and systemic driver

local.text: Remove trigger when possible; potent topical or intralesional corticosteroid for limited lesions; analgesia and ocular assessment if symptomatic.

systemic.text: Systemic glucocorticoid is typical for widespread, painful, febrile, or organ-involving disease; response is often rapid.

refractory.text: Colchicine, dapsone, potassium iodide, or other steroid-sparing therapy; treat malignancy/inflammatory driver. Re-biopsy if atypical or nonresponsive.

local.text: Gentle moisture-balanced wound care, atraumatic dressings, analgesia, edema control, topical/intralesional anti-inflammatory therapy for limited superficial disease; avoid unnecessary debridement.

systemic.text: Prednisolone or ciclosporin are established initial systemic options; select according to renal/BP risk, infection risk, diabetes, and comorbidity.

refractory.text: TNF inhibition—especially with IBD—or other biologic/immunosuppressive therapy in expert care; control associated disease and reassess infection/vascular mimics.

local.text: Antihistamines are often less effective than in ordinary urticaria because the process is neutrophilic rather than mast-cell dominant.

systemic.text: Dapsone or colchicine can suppress neutrophilic inflammation; monitor drug-specific toxicity.

refractory.text: Treat the underlying IL-1–mediated, Still, Schnitzler, CAPS, or lupus phenotype; IL-1 blockade may be decisive in selected disease.

local.text: Topical or intralesional corticosteroid for limited symptomatic lesions.

systemic.text: Hydroxychloroquine, dapsone, or another systemic anti-inflammatory agent may be used case by case.

refractory.text: Optimize treatment of RA, lupus, vasculitis, malignancy, infection, or medication trigger; response often follows control of the driver.

local.text: Exclude bacterial/fungal infection and manage local erosions or crusting.

systemic.text: Systemic glucocorticoid is often effective; dapsone, colchicine, hydroxychloroquine, or immunosuppressive therapy may be used.

refractory.text: Control associated SLE or autoimmune disease and reconsider IgA pemphigus, pustular psoriasis, and infection.

citations.quote: Review classifies neutrophilic dermatoses by clinical and histopathologic pattern and emphasizes exclusion of infection and systemic associations.
STOP GAP randomized trial compared prednisolone and ciclosporin as initial systemic therapy for pyoderma gangrenosum.
Review defines neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis as transient, usually nonpruritic lesions with dermal neutrophilia, leukocytoclasia, and no vasculitis.
A 65-patient series supports reactive granulomatous dermatitis as an umbrella for IGD, PNGD, and related patterns with frequent systemic associations.
